title: The Fox and the Wolf at the River

plan.english: In winter a fox was carrying fish by the water. A hungry wolf saw her and asked: "Where did you catch the fish?" She answered: "I put my tail in the water, and the fish bit it." Then the wolf went to the river and put his tail in it. He sat there the whole night, and the water became ice. In the morning the wolf pulled hard at his tail, and it stayed in the ice. Then the shepherds came with dogs, and the wolf left his tail there and fled. Do not listen to the words of a fox.

clauses.english: In winter a fox was carrying fish by the water.
A hungry wolf saw her and asked: "Where did you catch the fish?"
She answered: "I put my tail in the water, and the fish bit it."
Then the wolf went to the river and put his tail in it.
He sat there the whole night, and the water became ice.
In the morning the wolf pulled hard at his tail, and it stayed in the ice.
Then the shepherds came with dogs, and the wolf left his tail there and fled.
Do not listen to the words of a fox.

plan.english: A bird's nest was in a high tree. Three eggs lay in it. A black snake was creeping toward the nest. The mother saw the snake and cried out. An eagle heard her voice. He came down from the sky, seized the snake and carried it off. The eggs stayed whole, and her young grew up. A small bird has a strong friend.

clauses.english: A bird's nest was in a high tree.
Three eggs lay in it.
A black snake was creeping toward the nest.
The mother saw the snake and cried out.
An eagle heard her voice.
He came down from the sky, seized the snake and carried it off.
The eggs stayed whole, and her young grew up.
A small bird has a strong friend.

title: The Old Oak by the River

plan.english: An old oak stands by the lake. Its roots drink the water. Sparrows sit in its branches and sing. In summer the cattle lie in its shade. Then a great wind came from the hills. It broke many trees, and the oak was still standing. Its roots were deep in the earth. Deep roots do not fear the wind.

clauses.english: An old oak stands by the lake.
Its roots drink the water.
Sparrows sit in its branches and sing.
In summer the cattle lie in its shade.
Then a great wind came from the hills.
It broke many trees, and the oak was still standing.
Its roots were deep in the earth.
Deep roots do not fear the wind.

plan.english: Fire and water were fighting. Fire said: "I am stronger than you, because I eat the trees." Water said: "I am stronger, because I kill you." Then the two of them went to a wise old woman. She said: "Men live by water and by fire." "Water, stay in the river; fire, stay on the hearth." Now fire lives on the hearth, and water flows in the river.

clauses.english: Fire and water were fighting.
Fire said: "I am stronger than you, because I eat the trees."
Water said: "I am stronger, because I kill you."
Then the two of them went to a wise old woman.
She said: "Men live by water and by fire."
"Water, stay in the river; fire, stay on the hearth."
Now fire lives on the hearth, and water flows in the river.

title: The Young Man at the Ford

plan.english: A young man came to a deep river. He did not know the ford. He went into the water, and the water carried him off. An old woman was sitting there. She stretched out a branch to him, and he seized the branch. She pulled him out of the water. Then she said: "Young man, why did you not ask the elders?" He answered: "Mother, I did not know the ford; now I know it." He who asks the elders does not die in the water.

clauses.english: A young man came to a deep river.
He did not know the ford.
He went into the water, and the water carried him off.
An old woman was sitting there.
She stretched out a branch to him, and he seized the branch.
She pulled him out of the water.
Then she said: "Young man, why did you not ask the elders?"
He answered: "Mother, I did not know the ford; now I know it."
He who asks the elders does not die in the water.

plan.english: I eat wood, and I have no mouth. I do not drink water, and water kills me. At night I am red, and people sit around me. In winter everyone loves me. What am I? Fire.

clauses.english: I eat wood, and I have no mouth.
I do not drink water, and water kills me.
At night I am red, and people sit around me.
In winter everyone loves me.
What am I?
Fire.

title: A Riddle of the House Without a Door

plan.english: There is a small white house, and it has no door. A mother sits on it and warms it. A child sleeps inside it. When it wakes up, it breaks the house and comes out. What is it? An egg.

clauses.english: There is a small white house, and it has no door.
A mother sits on it and warms it.
A child sleeps inside it.
When it wakes up, it breaks the house and comes out.
What is it?
An egg.

title: A Riddle of the One Who Stands

plan.english: I stand, and I do not walk. My feet drink water under the earth. Birds build their nests in my hands. In summer I wear leaves, and in winter the snow covers me. Say my name. A tree.

clauses.english: I stand, and I do not walk.
My feet drink water under the earth.
Birds build their nests in my hands.
In summer I wear leaves, and in winter the snow covers me.
Say my name.
A tree.

plan.english: A dog was carrying meat, and he crossed a river. He looked into the water and caught sight of another dog. That one too was carrying meat, and his meat was bigger. He wanted that one. He bit the dog in the water, and his meat fell from his mouth. The water carried it off, and he had nothing. He who wants another's meat lets his own go.

clauses.english: A dog was carrying meat, and he crossed a river.
He looked into the water and caught sight of another dog.
That one too was carrying meat, and his meat was bigger.
He wanted that one.
He bit the dog in the water, and his meat fell from his mouth.
The water carried it off, and he had nothing.
He who wants another's meat lets his own go.

title: The Fox and the Black Bird

plan.english: A black bird was sitting in a tree, and she was carrying meat in her mouth. A fox went under the tree and caught sight of it. She said: "You are beautiful; is your voice sweet too?" "Sing to me!" The bird became glad and sang. The meat fell from her mouth, and the fox took it. The fox laughed. "Your voice is good, and your mind is small."

clauses.english: A black bird was sitting in a tree, and she was carrying meat in her mouth.
A fox went under the tree and caught sight of it.
She said: "You are beautiful; is your voice sweet too?"
"Sing to me!"
The bird became glad and sang.
The meat fell from her mouth, and the fox took it.
The fox laughed.
"Your voice is good, and your mind is small."

plan.english: A wolf was drinking water, and a lamb was drinking lower down. The wolf said: "Why are you stirring up my water?" The lamb said: "The water flows from you to me." Then he said: "Last year you spoke against me." The lamb said: "Last year I was not alive." The wolf seized the lamb and devoured him. A wolf does not listen to the words of a lamb.

clauses.english: A wolf was drinking water, and a lamb was drinking lower down.
The wolf said: "Why are you stirring up my water?"
The lamb said: "The water flows from you to me."
Then he said: "Last year you spoke against me."
The lamb said: "Last year I was not alive."
The wolf seized the lamb and devoured him.
A wolf does not listen to the words of a lamb.

plan.english: A great serpent lay on the mountain, and he was holding the waters. The rivers did not flow, and the fields were dry. Men and cattle were thirsty. Then Perkunos took his stone and came to the mountain. He slew the serpent, and the stone split the mountain. The waters came forth and flowed into the fields. Men praised Perkunos, the slayer of the serpent.

clauses.english: A great serpent lay on the mountain, and he was holding the waters.
The rivers did not flow, and the fields were dry.
Men and cattle were thirsty.
Then Perkunos took his stone and came to the mountain.
He slew the serpent, and the stone split the mountain.
The waters came forth and flowed into the fields.
Men praised Perkunos, the slayer of the serpent.

plan.english: An old man said to his son: "A small fire burns many trees." "Silent water is deep." "Do not carry fire in your hand." The son did not listen: he carried fire in his hand, and his hand burned. Now he knows his father's words.

clauses.english: An old man said to his son:
"A small fire burns many trees."
"Silent water is deep."
"Do not carry fire in your hand."
The son did not listen: he carried fire in his hand, and his hand burned.
Now he knows his father's words.

plan.english: A bear caught a hare in the field. The hare said: "Bear, I am small, and I shall not fill your belly." "A big sheep is grazing on the hill." "Let me go, and I will show you the sheep." The bear let the hare go, and the hare ran away. The bear went to the hill, and he found no sheep. A hare in the hand is better than a sheep on the hill.

clauses.english: A bear caught a hare in the field.
The hare said: "Bear, I am small, and I shall not fill your belly."
"A big sheep is grazing on the hill."
"Let me go, and I will show you the sheep."
The bear let the hare go, and the hare ran away.
The bear went to the hill, and he found no sheep.
A hare in the hand is better than a sheep on the hill.

title: A Riddle of the Walker in the Sky

plan.english: By day he walks across the sky, and at night he goes under the earth. His eye is bright, and no one looks at him. He warms the fields and dries the water. Who is he? The sun.

clauses.english: By day he walks across the sky, and at night he goes under the earth.
His eye is bright, and no one looks at him.
He warms the fields and dries the water.
Who is he?
The sun.

title: The Shepherd and the Frozen Snake

plan.english: In winter a shepherd found a snake in the snow. The snake was freezing and was lying on the ground. The shepherd carried it to his house and laid it by the hearth. The fire warmed the snake, and it woke up. Then the snake bit the shepherd, and the shepherd died. Do not warm a snake.

clauses.english: In winter a shepherd found a snake in the snow.
The snake was freezing and was lying on the ground.
The shepherd carried it to his house and laid it by the hearth.
The fire warmed the snake, and it woke up.
Then the snake bit the shepherd, and the shepherd died.
Do not warm a snake.

title: The Sparrow on the High Branch

plan.english: A sparrow was sitting on a high branch. A fox arrived and said: "Sparrow, come down; let us be friends." The sparrow answered: "I see dogs on the path; they are coming to you." She became afraid and ran away. There were no dogs, and the sparrow laughed. The fox's words are sweet, and her heart is bad.

clauses.english: A sparrow was sitting on a high branch.
A fox arrived and said: "Sparrow, come down; let us be friends."
The sparrow answered: "I see dogs on the path; they are coming to you."
She became afraid and ran away.
There were no dogs, and the sparrow laughed.
The fox's words are sweet, and her heart is bad.

plan.english: At night a young man caught sight of the moon in the water. He said: "I will take the moon out of the water." He put his hands into the water, and the moon vanished. When he drew his hands out, the moon was there again. An old woman was watching the young man, and she laughed. She said: "Young man, the moon is in the sky, and in the water is its shadow." "Do not grasp at shadows."

clauses.english: At night a young man caught sight of the moon in the water.
He said: "I will take the moon out of the water."
He put his hands into the water, and the moon vanished.
When he drew his hands out, the moon was there again.
An old woman was watching the young man, and she laughed.
She said: "Young man, the moon is in the sky, and in the water is its shadow."
"Do not grasp at shadows."

title: A Riddle of the One Who Goes on His Belly

plan.english: Tell me, who goes on his belly? He has no feet, and he runs quickly over the earth. In summer he leaves his old skin and wears a new one. His tooth kills, and people fear him. He is the snake.

clauses.english: Tell me, who goes on his belly?
He has no feet, and he runs quickly over the earth.
In summer he leaves his old skin and wears a new one.
His tooth kills, and people fear him.
He is the snake.

plan.english: The old woman said to the young men: "The feet of the young are swift, and the words of the old are wise." "The wolf is strong, and the fox knows many things." "A young tree bends, and an old tree breaks." "Listen to the old, and you will live for a long time." Then the young men were silent and listened.

clauses.english: The old woman said to the young men:
"The feet of the young are swift, and the words of the old are wise."
"The wolf is strong, and the fox knows many things."
"A young tree bends, and an old tree breaks."
"Listen to the old, and you will live for a long time."
Then the young men were silent and listened.

plan.english: Men had no fire, and they were cold in winter. A white bird flew to the sun. She took fire from the sun and brought it to the earth. The fire burned her wings, and they became black. Now she is black, and men sit at the fire. They praise her and do not kill her.

clauses.english: Men had no fire, and they were cold in winter.
A white bird flew to the sun.
She took fire from the sun and brought it to the earth.
The fire burned her wings, and they became black.
Now she is black, and men sit at the fire.
They praise her and do not kill her.

title: A Riddle of the Night Walker

plan.english: She grows great, and again she becomes small. She walks at night, and the stars follow her. She has no fire, and yet she becomes bright. Who is she? She is the moon.

clauses.english: She grows great, and again she becomes small.
She walks at night, and the stars follow her.
She has no fire, and yet she becomes bright.
Who is she?
She is the moon.

plan.english: A goat went to the field and said to its young one: "Do not open the door to anyone." Then the wolf came to the door and said: "Open the door; I am your mother." The young one said: "Show me your foot." The wolf showed his foot, and the foot was black. "My mother's feet are white; you are the wolf." The young one did not open the door, and the hungry wolf went away.

clauses.english: A goat went to the field and said to its young one:
"Do not open the door to anyone."
Then the wolf came to the door and said: "Open the door; I am your mother."
The young one said: "Show me your foot."
The wolf showed his foot, and the foot was black.
"My mother's feet are white; you are the wolf."
The young one did not open the door, and the hungry wolf went away.

plan.english: A young shepherd was guarding sheep on the hill. He cried out: "The wolf is coming!" The villagers came, and there was no wolf. The shepherd laughed, because he had deceived them. Then a wolf arrived, and the shepherd cried out again. The villagers heard his voice, and they did not come. The wolf killed many sheep. Do not deceive people, or they will not hear you.

clauses.english: A young shepherd was guarding sheep on the hill.
He cried out: "The wolf is coming!"
The villagers came, and there was no wolf.
The shepherd laughed, because he had deceived them.
Then a wolf arrived, and the shepherd cried out again.
The villagers heard his voice, and they did not come.
The wolf killed many sheep.
Do not deceive people, or they will not hear you.

title: The Snake Who Wished to Fly

plan.english: A snake spoke to an eagle: "Carry me to the sky!" The eagle said: "Snakes do not fly." The snake pleaded, and the eagle seized the snake with his feet and flew up. Then the eagle let the snake go, and the snake fell on a rock and died. The path of the snake is on the earth, and the path of the bird is in the sky.

clauses.english: A snake spoke to an eagle: "Carry me to the sky!"
The eagle said: "Snakes do not fly."
The snake pleaded, and the eagle seized the snake with his feet and flew up.
Then the eagle let the snake go, and the snake fell on a rock and died.
The path of the snake is on the earth, and the path of the bird is in the sky.

plan.english: A wolf was eating, and a bone stayed in his throat. He said to a crane: "Pull the bone out, and I will give you a reward." The crane put its head into the wolf's mouth and pulled out the bone. Then the crane asked: "Where is my reward?" The wolf answered: "You put your head in my mouth, and I did not bite it." "That is your reward." Do not seek a reward from a wolf.

clauses.english: A wolf was eating, and a bone stayed in his throat.
He said to a crane: "Pull the bone out, and I will give you a reward."
The crane put its head into the wolf's mouth and pulled out the bone.
Then the crane asked: "Where is my reward?"
The wolf answered: "You put your head in my mouth, and I did not bite it."
"That is your reward."
Do not seek a reward from a wolf.

plan.english: I am born from fire, and I climb up. I have no wings, and yet I fly over the trees. Women weep when they see me, and the wind drives me away. Who is my father, and what am I? Your father is fire, and you are smoke.

clauses.english: I am born from fire, and I climb up.
I have no wings, and yet I fly over the trees.
Women weep when they see me, and the wind drives me away.
Who is my father, and what am I?
Your father is fire, and you are smoke.

title: A Riddle of the Unseen One

plan.english: No one sees him, and all hear him. He has no hands, and yet he breaks the trees. He drives the clouds and stirs up the sea. In summer he is warm, and in winter he is cold. Who is this? The wind.

clauses.english: No one sees him, and all hear him.
He has no hands, and yet he breaks the trees.
He drives the clouds and stirs up the sea.
In summer he is warm, and in winter he is cold.
Who is this?
The wind.

plan.english: It runs by day and by night, and it does not become tired. It has no legs, and yet it goes to the sea. Fish live in it, and cattle drink from it. What is it? It is the river.

clauses.english: It runs by day and by night, and it does not become tired.
It has no legs, and yet it goes to the sea.
Fish live in it, and cattle drink from it.
What is it?
It is the river.

title: The Thirsty Bird and the Pot

plan.english: A thirsty bird found a pot. There was a little water in the pot, and the pot was deep. She considered, and she brought pebbles. She threw them into the pot, and the water came up. Then she drank, and she flew away. The wise one finds a path.

clauses.english: A thirsty bird found a pot.
There was a little water in the pot, and the pot was deep.
She considered, and she brought pebbles.
She threw them into the pot, and the water came up.
Then she drank, and she flew away.
The wise one finds a path.

plan.english: A she-wolf caught a goose by the lake. The goose said: "Let me sing a song; then eat me." The she-wolf let the goose go and sat down. The goose spread her wings and flew up into the tree. From the tree she sang: "She-wolf, now you will not eat the goose." What you hold, do not let it go.

clauses.english: A she-wolf caught a goose by the lake.
The goose said: "Let me sing a song; then eat me."
The she-wolf let the goose go and sat down.
The goose spread her wings and flew up into the tree.
From the tree she sang: "She-wolf, now you will not eat the goose."
What you hold, do not let it go.

title: The Old Woman and the Thief

plan.english: At night a thief arrived at the house of an old woman. The woman was awake, and she heard him. She spoke to her son: "Our gold is under the old tree." The thief heard this and went to the tree. He dug the whole night, and he found nothing. In the morning the villagers seized the thief. She laughed: "The tree has no gold, and the thief has no sleep."

clauses.english: At night a thief arrived at the house of an old woman.
The woman was awake, and she heard him.
She spoke to her son: "Our gold is under the old tree."
The thief heard this and went to the tree.
He dug the whole night, and he found nothing.
In the morning the villagers seized the thief.
She laughed: "The tree has no gold, and the thief has no sleep."

title: The Tree Between Earth and Sky

plan.english: In the middle of the earth stands a great tree. Its roots drink from the deep waters, and its branches hold up the sky. An eagle sits at its top, and a serpent lies at its roots. The serpent eats the roots, and the eagle fights against him. If the serpent devours all the roots, the tree will fall, and the sky will fall. The eagle watches the serpent by day and by night.

clauses.english: In the middle of the earth stands a great tree.
Its roots drink from the deep waters, and its branches hold up the sky.
An eagle sits at its top, and a serpent lies at its roots.
The serpent eats the roots, and the eagle fights against him.
If the serpent devours all the roots, the tree will fall, and the sky will fall.
The eagle watches the serpent by day and by night.

plan.english: A beaver and an otter lived in a lake. All summer the beaver was working: he was cutting wood and building a house. The otter was playing in the lake and was merry. She said: "Why are you working? The summer is long." The beaver said: "Rain will come, and the water will become great." In autumn it rained for many days. The lake became full, and it carried off the otter's home. The beaver's house stood, and he slept in it. He who works in summer sleeps in a warm house in winter.

clauses.english: A beaver and an otter lived in a lake.
All summer the beaver was working: he was cutting wood and building a house.
The otter was playing in the lake and was merry.
She said: "Why are you working? The summer is long."
The beaver said: "Rain will come, and the water will become great."
In autumn it rained for many days.
The lake became full, and it carried off the otter's home.
The beaver's house stood, and he slept in it.
He who works in summer sleeps in a warm house in winter.

plan.english: A grandfather was sitting at the hearth with the children, and he said: "A guest at the hearth is holy." "Give the guest milk and honey, and he will praise you." "Do not pour water into the fire." "When the hearth is cold, the house is sad." "Feed the fire with dry wood, and it will warm you." The children listened, and the fire burned.

clauses.english: A grandfather was sitting at the hearth with the children, and he said:
"A guest at the hearth is holy."
"Give the guest milk and honey, and he will praise you."
"Do not pour water into the fire."
"When the hearth is cold, the house is sad."
"Feed the fire with dry wood, and it will warm you."
The children listened, and the fire burned.

title: A Riddle of the White One

plan.english: I am white, and I come down from the clouds. I cover the fields and the trees, and I am silent. Children play with me; when the sun comes, I become water. Who am I? Snow.

clauses.english: I am white, and I come down from the clouds.
I cover the fields and the trees, and I am silent.
Children play with me; when the sun comes, I become water.
Who am I?
Snow.

plan.english: A grandfather said to a boy: "Listen, boy, and answer." "What is swifter than the wind?" The boy said: "Thought is swifter." "What is sweeter than honey?" "Sleep is sweeter." "What is deeper than the sea?" The boy was silent, and he did not know. The grandfather said: "Grief is deeper than the sea." "May you not know it for a long time."

clauses.english: A grandfather said to a boy: "Listen, boy, and answer."
"What is swifter than the wind?"
The boy said: "Thought is swifter."
"What is sweeter than honey?"
"Sleep is sweeter."
"What is deeper than the sea?"
The boy was silent, and he did not know.
The grandfather said: "Grief is deeper than the sea."
"May you not know it for a long time."

title: The Duck and the Golden Eggs

plan.english: A man had a duck, and every day she brought forth an egg of gold. The man said: "There is much gold in her belly." He took a knife and cut her open. There was no gold in the belly, and the duck was dead. Now the man had no duck, and he had no eggs. He who wants much has nothing.

clauses.english: A man had a duck, and every day she brought forth an egg of gold.
The man said: "There is much gold in her belly."
He took a knife and cut her open.
There was no gold in the belly, and the duck was dead.
Now the man had no duck, and he had no eggs.
He who wants much has nothing.

plan.english: The god Fire became afraid and fled into the waters. He hid himself there, and the hearths of men were cold. The gods sought Fire in the sea and in the rivers. A fish saw him and said to the gods: "Fire lies in the deep water." The gods led Fire out and set him on the hearth. Fire was angry with the fish, and he said: "Men will kill you with sharp knives." Now they catch fish and kill them.

clauses.english: The god Fire became afraid and fled into the waters.
He hid himself there, and the hearths of men were cold.
The gods sought Fire in the sea and in the rivers.
A fish saw him and said to the gods: "Fire lies in the deep water."
The gods led Fire out and set him on the hearth.
Fire was angry with the fish, and he said: "Men will kill you with sharp knives."
Now they catch fish and kill them.

plan.english: The sun and the wind spoke: "Which of us is stronger?" A man was walking on the path, and he was wearing a garment. The wind said: "I will snatch his garment from him." The wind blew, and the man held on to his garment. Then the sun became bright, and the man was sweating. He threw his garment away and lay down in the shade. The wind was silent, and the sun became glad. Warmth is stronger than the wind.

clauses.english: The sun and the wind spoke: "Which of us is stronger?"
A man was walking on the path, and he was wearing a garment.
The wind said: "I will snatch his garment from him."
The wind blew, and the man held on to his garment.
Then the sun became bright, and the man was sweating.
He threw his garment away and lay down in the shade.
The wind was silent, and the sun became glad.
Warmth is stronger than the wind.
